rows.limit: t -> 0: the body has not moved
rows.why: over 1 ns a body with a 1125 s time constant cannot move measurably; T(0+) -> T_0 because exp(0) = 1

rows.limit: t -> infinity: the body reaches steady state
rows.why: the exponential dies, leaving T_amb + Q/hA

rows.limit: Q -> 0 and t -> infinity: the body reaches ambient
rows.why: an unheated body equilibrates with its ambient, not above it

rows.limit: hA -> large: the body is clamped to ambient
rows.why: infinite conductance is a perfect thermal short to the ambient

rows.limit: hA -> 0: adiabatic heating at Q/C
rows.why: with no loss path the body integrates Q/C linearly in time

rows.invariant: more heat in -> higher final temperature
more conductance -> a hot body cools closer to ambient
more thermal mass -> slower approach, so closer to T_0 at fixed t

rows.case: nominal Li-ion half hour
rows.oracle: z = z0 - I t / (eta Q_nom), charge conservation
rows.why: exact algebra on both sides, but the unit conversion differs: the oracle divides by an explicit 3600 and the Core converts through its unit system, so a scaling slip in either is visible

rows.case: nominal Li-ion half hour: OCV on the chord
rows.oracle: OCV = V_e + (V_f - V_e) z
rows.why: affine interpolation, exact

rows.case: nominal Li-ion half hour: terminal voltage
rows.oracle: KVL: V = OCV - I R
rows.why: Kirchhoff's voltage law around the Rint loop

rows.case: nominal Li-ion half hour: Joule heat
rows.oracle: P = I^2 R
rows.why: Joule's law; must be non-negative for either current direction

rows.case: nominal Li-ion half hour: charge balance
rows.oracle: (z0 - z_end) eta Q_nom * 3600 == I t, in coulombs
rows.why: the electrons the model says left the cell must be the electrons the load drew. Passes on the relative residual, or on the floating-point cancellation floor of the difference z0 - z_end when almost no charge moved

rows.limit: I -> 0: the terminal voltage is the open-circuit voltage
rows.why: with no current there is no IR drop, by definition of open circuit

rows.limit: I -> 0: no charge leaves the cell
rows.why: zero current for any time removes zero charge

rows.limit: R -> 0: the cell becomes ideal and V -> OCV
rows.why: a zero series resistance drops no voltage

rows.case: a charging current at the public constructor
rows.invariant: a discharge-only model must not silently compute a charge
rows.why: the record excludes charging and says no condition would catch one; the constructor closes that gap ahead of the conditions by refusing the declaration

rows.case: zero current at the public constructor
rows.invariant: a discharge-only model must not silently compute a charge

rows.case: discharge lowers the terminal voltage below OCV
rows.invariant: V < OCV for I > 0, V > OCV for I < 0
rows.why: the IR drop opposes the current, so a discharge always pulls the terminal below the open circuit; a sign slip here inverts the whole model and would still look like a plausible voltage

rows.case: divider: V(a) against an incidence-matrix nodal solve

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: beta = (-dH)/(rho cp)
rows.oracle: definition
rows.why: the adiabatic temperature rise per unit concentration

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: gamma = UA/(V rho cp)
rows.oracle: definition
rows.why: the jacket cooling rate constant

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: final C_A
rows.oracle: explicit fixed-step RK4, Jacobian-free
rows.why: RK4 at 600k steps is far inside its own error here; the tolerance is set by the oracle's resolution, not by the accuracy anyone wants the Core to have

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: final T
rows.oracle: explicit fixed-step RK4, Jacobian-free
rows.why: same integration, temperature channel

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: the endpoint sits on an algebraic steady state
rows.oracle: bisection on F(T) = 0 with C_A = a C_Af/(a + k(T)); no time integration at all
rows.why: an independent route of a different KIND: algebra rather than integration. A long run must land on a root of the steady-state equation

rows.case: cooled, from the feed state: the invariant ceiling on T
rows.oracle: Z = T + beta C_A obeys dZ/dt = a(Z_f - Z) - gamma(T - T_c); the reaction term cancels
rows.why: an exact bound the trajectory cannot cross, derived by adding beta times the species balance to the energy balance. It holds for any rate law, so it tests the COUPLING rather than the kinetics

rows.limit: k -> 0: no reaction, so the outlet is the feed
rows.why: with no consumption the tank washes out to the feed concentration

rows.limit: k -> 0: temperature is the flow/jacket weighted mean
rows.why: setting dT/dt = 0 with no reaction gives a(T_f - T) = gamma(T - T_c), whose solution is (a T_f + gamma T_c)/(a + gamma). Derived here

rows.limit: UA -> 0: adiabatic, so T rises by beta times the conversion
rows.why: an exothermic reaction with no cooling cannot leave the tank colder than its feed

rows.case: endothermic reaction (dH > 0) with no jacket
rows.invariant: an endothermic reaction absorbs heat and lowers the temperature
rows.why: beta = (-dH)/(rho cp) changes sign with the enthalpy of reaction. A model that heated on an endotherm would have the single most consequential sign in reactor engineering backwards, and would still return entirely plausible temperatures

rows.invariant: a warmer jacket leaves a warmer reactor
rows.why: the cooling term pulls T towards T_c
a faster rate constant consumes more reactant at the same residence time

rows.case: terminal voltage developed across a 10 mA source into 470 ohm
rows.oracle: Ohm's law on the injected current, derived here: V = I R = 4.7 V
rows.why: an ideal source imposes its current whatever voltage develops

rows.case: the same terminal voltage, against ngspice
rows.oracle: ngspice 42
rows.why: confirms the SPICE current-source sign convention matches this domain's

rows.case: a source driving current into a node raises that node
rows.invariant: current injected at `to_node` makes it positive w.r.t. the reference
rows.why: the domain declares current flowing from_node -> to_node INSIDE the source, so it is injected at to_node. Reversed, the node would go negative and every power sign would follow

rows.case: imposes the same v_pos - v_neg = V_src as the ideal source
rows.oracle: incidence-matrix nodal solve of the same circuit
rows.why: the regulated record differs from the ideal one in the BAND over which it asserts the relation, not in the relation. The equation checked here is therefore the same equation, verified rather than assumed to be shared

rows.case: element hot spot = T_body + P R_th
rows.oracle: one-dimensional conduction through a thermal resistance, derived here
rows.why: the utilization the record bounds is a ratio of absolute temperatures; its numerator is the body temperature plus the element's own rise. The dissipation it uses is the one checked against ngspice above

rows.case: final C_A with a temperature-independent rate constant
rows.oracle: explicit RK4 with k held constant, written in this audit
rows.why: the constant-rate model is the same kernel evaluated at E = 0, where the Arrhenius factor is exactly 1. That reduction is verified numerically here rather than taken on trust

rows.case: final T with a temperature-independent rate constant
rows.oracle: explicit RK4 with k held constant, written in this audit
rows.why: same integration, temperature channel

rows.limit: E -> 0: the Arrhenius factor is exactly 1 at every temperature
rows.why: this is what makes the constant-rate model reachable through the Arrhenius kernel at all; if exp(-0/(RT)) were not exactly 1 the two models would not be the same equation
